description: 45 fintech logos explained by a brand designer, from Stripe, PayPal, and Wise to Robinhood, Coinbase, Klarna, and Chime.
intro:
Fintech logos live inside app stores, on payment buttons, and on debit cards, so the best ones are trustworthy enough to hold your money and friendly enough to open every day.

What makes a good fintech logo?

Trust without stiffness: fintech brands compete with traditional banks, so most use friendly lowercase wordmarks and soft shapes, like Stripe, Chime, and Coinbase, instead of heavy serif crests.

A shape that works as an app icon: the Cash App dollar, the PayPal double P, and the Square square are recognized on a phone screen without the name.

Color as a signature: Venmo blue, Robinhood green, Klarna pink, and Binance yellow make each brand instantly recognizable in a crowded wallet.

Below are 45 fintech logos in five groups, from payments and money transfer to investing apps, crypto, and neobanks. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation. For traditional and digital banks, see my review of bank logos.

logoResearch.name: Stripe
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Stripe is a payments infrastructure company used by millions of online businesses.
observations: A simple lowercase wordmark with no symbol, set in Stripe's signature purple-blue.
The heavy, slightly condensed letters feel solid and developer-friendly.

logoResearch.name: PayPal
logoResearch.verifiedFact: PayPal is one of the world's most widely used online payment platforms.
observations: Two overlapping P shapes in navy and blue form a monogram that works as an app icon.
The italic wordmark leans forward, suggesting fast payments.

logoResearch.name: Square
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Square is the payments and point-of-sale business of Block.
observations: A square inside a rounded square is the most literal logo in fintech.
The friendly, rounded wordmark matches the simple shape.

logoResearch.name: Adyen
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Adyen is a Dutch payments company that processes payments for large global businesses.
observations: A green lowercase wordmark with custom, connected letters.
The flat-topped letters look like they sit on a line, like a card terminal display.

logoResearch.name: Klarna
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Klarna is a Swedish buy now, pay later and shopping company.
observations: A bold, black wordmark with a custom K is the whole logo.
Klarna is known for its pink brand color, used around the logo rather than in it.

logoResearch.name: Affirm
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Affirm is a US buy now, pay later company.
observations: A curved line arches over the end of the name, like a smile or a rainbow.
Light lowercase letters keep the brand friendly and approachable.

logoResearch.name: Checkout.com
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Checkout.com is a London-based global payments company.
observations: A blue square with an abstract X-like symbol looks like a checkout button.
The .com is part of the name and the logo.

logoResearch.name: Venmo
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Venmo is a US mobile payment app owned by PayPal.
observations: A heavy, italic blue wordmark looks fast and casual.
The rounded, friendly letters match an app built for paying friends.

logoResearch.name: Cash App
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Cash App is Block's mobile payment and banking app.
observations: A green dollar sign in a black rounded square is the app icon and the logo.
The bold, simple symbol works at any size, from a phone screen to a debit card.

logoResearch.name: Wise
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Wise is a money transfer company, formerly called TransferWise.
observations: A flag-like arrow symbol points forward, like money moving across borders.
Heavy, italic capitals in dark green feel bold and confident.

logoResearch.name: Remitly
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Remitly is a digital remittance company for sending money internationally.
observations: A shield shape with a handshake-like line suggests trust and protection.
A rounded navy wordmark keeps it approachable.

logoResearch.name: Payoneer
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Payoneer is a cross-border payments company for businesses and freelancers.
observations: A rainbow gradient ring stands for a global, connected network.
A heavy black wordmark grounds the colorful symbol.

logoResearch.name: Airwallex
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Airwallex is a global business payments and financial platform founded in Australia.
observations: An orange-red loop like an infinity sign suggests money flowing without limits.
A bold wordmark keeps the long name compact.

logoResearch.name: Rapyd
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Rapyd is a global payments and fintech-as-a-service company.
observations: Heavy italic letters lean forward to suggest speed, a nod to the name.
The custom y gives the wordmark its own detail.

logoResearch.name: dLocal
logoResearch.verifiedFact: dLocal is a Uruguayan payments company for emerging markets.
observations: A middle dot splits d and local, like a location point on a map.
Heavy, rounded lowercase letters feel friendly and solid.

logoResearch.name: Xe
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Xe is a currency data and money transfer company.
observations: Two letters inside a ring look like a coin or a currency symbol.
The short name makes one of the most compact logos in fintech.

logoResearch.name: Western Union
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Western Union is a 170-year-old money transfer company.
observations: Yellow letters on black are among the most recognizable colors in finance.
The WU monogram works on its own at small sizes.

logoResearch.name: Ebury
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Ebury is a London-based payments and FX company for small and mid-sized businesses.
observations: A lowercase wordmark with a looping y is the whole logo.
Dark, friendly letters keep the brand simple.

logoResearch.name: Robinhood
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Robinhood is a commission-free investing and trading app.
observations: A feather symbol nods to Robin Hood's hat and the idea of giving finance to everyone.
A light, modern wordmark keeps the app feeling approachable.

logoResearch.name: Webull
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Webull is a trading and investing platform.
observations: A curved shape like a smile or a rising arc sits beside the name.
Bold, rounded letters keep the brand modern.

logoResearch.name: Acorns
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Acorns is a micro-investing app that invests spare change.
observations: A green acorn is a symbol of small things growing into big ones.
A rounded lowercase wordmark in the same green feels friendly.

logoResearch.name: eToro
logoResearch.verifiedFact: eToro is a social trading and investing platform.
observations: Green angle brackets wrap the name, like code or a ticker.
The light lowercase letters make trading feel friendly.

logoResearch.name: Public
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Public is an investing platform for stocks, bonds, and crypto.
observations: A small blue dot above a stem looks like a person or a pin.
A simple lowercase wordmark keeps the brand quiet.

logoResearch.name: Wealthfront
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Wealthfront is an automated investing and savings platform.
observations: Stacked strokes form a small mark like rising bars or a W.
A bold, heavy wordmark feels confident and stable.

logoResearch.name: Betterment
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Betterment is a US robo-advisor and investing platform.
observations: A yellow half-circle looks like a rising sun, a symbol of a better future.
A bold navy wordmark balances the bright symbol.

logoResearch.name: Stash
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Stash is a US investing and banking app.
observations: Custom, angular capitals with cut strokes give the name a distinctive shape.
The black, wide letters make the brand bold.

logoResearch.name: Trading 212
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Trading 212 is a European investing app.
observations: An upward caret replaces the A, like a rising stock chart.
A tagline, Build wealth every day, sits under the name.

logoResearch.name: Coinbase
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Coinbase is the largest US cryptocurrency exchange.
observations: A bright blue, rounded lowercase wordmark is the whole logo.
The round letters echo the shape of a coin.

logoResearch.name: Kraken
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Kraken is a US cryptocurrency exchange.
observations: A small purple sea monster mark sits next to the name.
A light purple lowercase wordmark is unusual and memorable.

logoResearch.name: Binance
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Binance is the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume.
observations: A yellow diamond made of smaller diamonds looks like a coin or a gem.
Wide yellow capitals match the symbol.

logoResearch.name: Circle
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Circle is the issuer of the USDC stablecoin.
observations: A gradient ring with a cut looks like a coin in motion.
Spaced capitals give the brand a calm, institutional feel.

logoResearch.name: Ripple
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Ripple is a crypto and blockchain payments company.
observations: Three connected blue dots form a network or a ripple spreading out.
A bold lowercase wordmark keeps it friendly.

logoResearch.name: Phantom
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Phantom is a crypto wallet app.
observations: A purple ghost is a playful, literal symbol of the name.
A rounded purple wordmark matches the friendly mascot.

logoResearch.name: MetaMask
logoResearch.verifiedFact: MetaMask is a popular crypto wallet.
observations: The wordmark uses heavy, custom letters with sharp angles.
MetaMask is known for its fox symbol, used separately from this wordmark.

logoResearch.name: Ledger
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Ledger is a French maker of hardware wallets for crypto.
observations: Corner brackets frame the name like a camera viewfinder or a secure box.
Thin capitals inside the frame feel precise and secure.

logoResearch.name: Gemini
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Gemini is a US cryptocurrency exchange founded by the Winklevoss twins.
observations: Two overlapping shapes form a G, a nod to the twins and to Gemini.
Spaced capitals keep the brand clean.

logoResearch.name: Chime
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Chime is a US financial technology company offering mobile banking.
observations: A soft, rounded lowercase wordmark in green.
The friendly look matches its positioning as banking without fees.

logoResearch.name: Starling Bank
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Starling Bank is a UK digital bank.
observations: Bold capitals in deep purple feel stable and trustworthy.
With no symbol, the name itself is the brand.

logoResearch.name: Dave
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Dave is a US neobank known for small cash advances.
observations: A heavy green wordmark with a playful, chunky shape.
Using a first name makes the bank feel like a friend.

logoResearch.name: Current
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Current is a US mobile banking app.
observations: Custom letters with a flat cut through the middle suggest a current or a wave.
Heavy black type makes the brand bold.

logoResearch.name: Varo
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Varo is a US digital bank.
observations: A purple wordmark with a gradient feels modern and energetic.
Short and rounded, the name works well as an app icon.

logoResearch.name: Credit Karma
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Credit Karma is a personal finance company owned by Intuit.
observations: A friendly green lowercase wordmark is the whole logo.
The light, open letters make credit scores feel less scary.

logoResearch.name: Lemonade
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Lemonade is an AI-driven insurance company.
observations: A flowing script wordmark looks hand-written and personal.
The playful script makes insurance feel human.

logoResearch.name: Upstart
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Upstart is an AI lending marketplace.
observations: A teal chevron points up, a direct symbol of the name.
A clean sans wordmark keeps the brand modern.

logoResearch.name: Marqeta
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Marqeta is a modern card issuing platform.
observations: Forward chevrons before the name suggest speed and movement.
Purple capitals feel bold and distinctive.

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 fintech logos in one consistent format, grouped into payments, money transfer, investing, crypto, and neobanks.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the product, fees, or financial performance.
sectionIntroductions: Payment brands appear on checkout buttons and terminals, so their logos are short, bold, and easy to recognize at a glance.
Money transfer companies sell speed and trust across borders, with forward-moving symbols and global color palettes.
Investing apps try to make the stock market feel approachable, with friendly type, bright colors, and growth symbols.
Crypto brands range from playful mascots to serious, institutional wordmarks, depending on who they want to reach.
Neobanks and consumer finance apps compete with big banks by looking friendlier, with rounded lowercase type and bright colors.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of fintech logos, not a ranking of financial products.
Look at how each logo balances trust with friendliness, and how it would look as an app icon.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo would look as an app icon and on a payment card.

findings.heading: Lowercase is the fintech default
findings.text: Stripe, Chime, Coinbase, Affirm, and public all use lowercase wordmarks to feel more approachable than traditional banks.

findings.heading: The best marks work as app icons
findings.text: The Cash App dollar, the PayPal double P, Square's square, and the Binance diamond are recognized on a phone screen without the name.

findings.heading: Color is a signature
findings.text: Venmo blue, Robinhood and Chime green, Klarna pink, and Binance yellow each own a color in a crowded category.

findings.heading: Growth symbols are everywhere
findings.text: Acorns' acorn, Betterment's rising sun, Upstart's chevron, and Trading 212's caret all point to money growing over time.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new fintech logo
checklistItems: Does the logo feel trustworthy enough to hold someone's money?
Is the symbol recognizable as a small app icon without the name?
Can you own one color in your category?
Does it look good on a debit card, a payment button, and a phone notification?
Is it friendly without looking like a toy?

faq.question: What makes a good fintech logo?
faq.answer: A good fintech logo balances trust with friendliness. The strongest examples, like Stripe, PayPal, and Cash App, use a simple shape or wordmark that works as an app icon, one signature color, and type that feels more approachable than a traditional bank.

faq.question: Why do so many fintech logos use lowercase letters?
faq.answer: Lowercase wordmarks feel friendlier and more modern than the serif capitals of traditional banks. Fintech brands like Stripe, Chime, Coinbase, and Affirm use them to signal that their product is simpler and easier to use.

faq.question: What colors do fintech brands use?
faq.answer: Fintech brands use a wider range of colors than banks. Blue still signals trust, but green suggests growth and money, while brighter colors like Klarna pink, Binance yellow, and Varo purple help apps stand out on a phone screen.
